exercises.objective: Recall RLEARN-00's control-stack-shortcuts framing from memory.
exercises.prompt: State RLEARN-00's 'shortcuts to the model-based control stack' framing in your own words, and give one concrete example pairing (a classical DYN/KIN component and the RLEARN module that shortcuts it).
hints: The framing: robot learning methods replace or shortcut specific pieces of the model-based stack (dynamics modeling, optimal control, constraint-solving, state estimation) when the assumptions behind that classical piece break down.
One example: dynamics modeling (DYN-01's M(q)q_ddot+F(q,q_dot)=u) shortcut by system identification/dynamics learning (RLEARN-01).

Another valid example: optimal control (DYN-04's Riccati/MPC) shortcut by learning a value/Q-function directly (RL-02/RL-03), or constraint-solving/IK (KIN-03) shortcut by a policy or sampler that directly satisfies the constraint.

exercises.objective: Name the privileged-teacher pattern and at least three modules that instantiate it.
exercises.prompt: Name the recurring pattern that connects RLEARN-02's DAgger, RLEARN-04's sim2real, and RLEARN-06's grasp labels, and explain the pattern in one sentence.
hints: All three involve some source of information available during training but not at deployment.

The pattern: train with information unavailable at deployment (a privileged expert, simulator, or exact-pose computation), generate labels/data from it, then train a deployment-time model on only what's actually available at deployment.
A fourth valid example: RLEARN-07's Deep Visual Constraints, trained on privileged simulation trial-and-error data but deployed using only camera images.
